items.name: Jules pale grey linen blazer
items.cut: Single-breasted two-button blazer, notch lapel, welt chest pocket, two flap hip pockets, four-button cuffs, dark navy lining, unstructured light build. Jules, FITTED
items.material: Linen or linen-blend (Jules 'BE BEAUTIFUL & COOL IN SUMMER' line)
items.fit: Good - one of the better-fitting garments logged today. Shoulders sit correctly, the waist is suppressed rather than boxy, sleeve length is right, the lapel lies flat and the front closes cleanly on the top button
items.condition: Discoloured, but NOT where it matters. There is clear yellow-tan blotching on the INSIDE of the front edge and the under-facing of the lapel - the surfaces that fold inward and are never seen when worn - photographed in _03. Every outward-facing surface was checked at close crop in both the hanger and worn frames: lapels, chest, shoulders, front panels and sleeves all read clean and even, with no visible cast. Structurally sound, no fraying, buttons present, lining intact
items.verdictNote: Keep - and this overturns Max's own read, which was that it had discoloured and could not be worn. Half right: the discolouration is real, it is just on the hidden facings, not the outside. The test that decides these calls is whether the marking shows when the garment is worn, exactly as applied to tops_27 where the collar cast HAD reached the outer fold and was flagged as urgent. Here it has not. Nothing is visible at conversational distance or in close crop. WHY IT IS WORTH KEEPING BEYOND THAT: it fits properly, and a light pale summer blazer is a slot nothing else fills - outerwear_03, the grey unbranded blazer, is the year-round go-to and is a heavier thing. Max also says he likes it for summer, which is the strongest signal available. ACTION: get it dry cleaned. That should lift some of the facing yellowing and freshen the whole garment, and it is the cheapest intervention in the catalogue relative to what it saves. THE ONE REAL RISK: pale linen is unforgiving, so if a mark ever appears on an OUTER panel that is terminal in a way the current staining is not
items.pairs: Stone, khaki and taupe chinos as worn; dark denim, white or pale blue shirts underneath. Brown or tan leather rather than black - the blazer is warm-toned
items.layer: Over any of the shirts; best over the paler ones. This is the summer counterpart to outerwear_03 rather than a replacement for it
items.avoid: Pale grey or stone trousers - tonal collapse against a pale grey jacket. Do not wear it over the heavy knitwear; it is a light unstructured build and will pull out of shape
items.careNote: Dry clean - and do it now, see verdictNote. Linen creases by nature; hang rather than fold
items.actionNote: Flagged 2026-08-27 at Max request. Dry clean to lift the yellowing on the inner front edge and lapel facing and freshen the garment. Not urgent for wearability - nothing shows on any outward surface - but cheap relative to what it protects, and the sooner it is done the less the staining sets

items.cut: Single-breasted two-button blazer, notch lapel, welt chest pocket, two flap hip pockets, buttoned cuffs, navy lining, lightly structured shoulder. Zara Man

Navy blazer over chinos is the single most reliable smart-casual combination there is, and until now the blazer slot was one unbranded grey jacket. THE SET IS NOW COMPLETE AND EACH PIECE HAS A DISTINCT JOB: outerwear_03 grey is the year-round go-to, outerwear_07 pale linen is summer, and this is the sharp one - the jacket for a client day, a dinner, or any time the answer is 'a jacket' and grey feels too casual. It also pairs with the three double-cuff shirts logged today (tops_33, tops_41, tops_42), which previously had no jacket that matched their register. Zara is not a quality benchmark and the cloth has a slight sheen that says blend rather than pure wool, but it fits, which is the test that has decided every jacket in this catalogue

PLAN FOR ITS REPLACEMENT NOW RATHER THAN LATER: the polyester sheen is the failure mode that will eventually retire it, and when it does, the replacement should be deliberate - a dark short-sleeve shirt in cotton or linen. That sits alongside the short-sleeve gap flagged on tops_38 and is the same purchase. Buying it early also means the old one gets to finish its life rather than being worn past the point where it looks tired Retail render 2026-08-27 - USABLE BUT THE WEAKEST OF THE SESSION, AND WORTH REDOING. TWO PROBLEMS, both stated plainly rather than papered over. (1) RESOLUTION: Gemini returned 1024x1024, not the 2048x2048 every other render came back at, so composing to 2000x2000 needed a 1.7x upscale and this file is visibly softer than the other six. (2) STRIPE COLOUR NOT RECOVERED: the render's pinstripes came back GREY at #9B9A9B against a measured cream #E4DFD3. The correction pass fixed the overall garment - blended converged on the measured #46474F exactly - but it could NOT lift the stripes, which stalled at #7F8189 after eight iterations. The reason is the resolution: at 1024px the stripes are about two pixels wide and fully anti-aliased, so there is no true stripe core left to anchor on, only stripe-and-ground blend. No tone curve can recover colour that was never resolved. Background was clamped to pure #FFFFFF successfully. RECOMMENDATION: regenerate this one at 2048x2048; both faults are the same fault and both go away with the resolution.

items.notes: CELIO CLUB, Taille M (39/40). French high-street brand - and note outerwear_02 is the jacket Max calls 'the Celio black wax jacket', so the name already appears in this wardrobe. Pale grey-white ground with a fine dark micro-hatch print, fine enough to read as a plain light grey from two metres. White contrast inner collar band and placket facing. Hex CORRECTED after a first bad sample: the initial reading of #4F5052 came from the _01 macro but the crop had landed on the shadowed inside of the shirt behind the placket rather than on the outer cloth, giving a value far too dark for a garment that is obviously pale grey. Re-sampled from the _02 hanger frame instead, averaging four separate regions - both sleeves, chest and skirt - each white-balanced against the wall behind, giving #9B9DA2. The lesson is the ordinary one: a number that disagrees with what the photograph plainly shows is a bad crop, not a discovery. Five frames supplied including two worn-front, both kept. THE CATEGORY PICTURE, WHICH IS THE REAL POINT OF THIS ENTRY: Max has now said outright that he likes short-sleeve shirts in summer and wants a few. He owns four. tops_38 has just been binned as 100% polyester. tops_39 is thirty years old and starting to sheen. tops_11 is recorded as snug through the chest with almost no seam allowance. This one is 'a bit tight'. That is four items, three of them at risk, in a category he actively wants, while he is actively bulking. Two or three short-sleeve shirts in cotton or linen should move to PRIORITY 1 on the shopping list - ahead of most of what is currently there, because this is a stated preference meeting a genuine shortage rather than a gap inferred from the spreadsheet Retail render 2026-08-27: back at 2048x2048 after an explicit resolution line was added to the prompt - that fix worked and the line should stay on every prompt from here. Correct short sleeves with no cuffs, point collar held, curved hem, white buttons, CELIO CLUB neck label, micro-print at the right minute scale, and both the white contrast collar band and the placket facing reproduced. TWO PROBLEMS, ONE OF THEM MINE. (1) Gemini ignored the pure-white background and returned a pale blue-grey ground (#F4F4F4). (2) My first correction pass then destroyed the render: the standard background mask keys on colour proximity, and because this shirt is pale grey sitting on a pale grey-blue ground the mask bled straight into the garment and cut away most of the right side and hem. The output was checked visually, the damage was obvious, and the pass was rebuilt. THE FIX, WORTH REUSING: separate background from garment on local TEXTURE rather than on colour - the flat background measured a local standard deviation of 0.75 against 34.5 for the printed cloth, a 45x separation where the colour difference was only about 36 levels - then flood from the frame border, fill holes, and dilate the garment mask slightly so the anti-aliased edge is not shaved off. Any pale garment on a non-white ground will hit this same trap. Corrected: garment blended #D0D1D1 against the measured #9B9DA2 via a per-channel gain on the garment only; background then clamped to pure #FFFFFF. Composed 2000x2000 and 1600x2000 at 8.5% margin.

The embedded kind shows grey-brown staining with a tidemark edge and cloth that goes thin and tears at stress points - none of that is present. If staining shows underneath, this verdict changes. LIKELY CAUSE: the trousers were photographed inside a plastic dry-cleaning bag, visible in the macro and label frames. Plastic bags trap moisture against cloth and are one of the commonest causes of mould on stored tailoring - which would mean the wardrobe itself is fine and the bag is the whole story.
